summary: LocalSequencerAncestorSealTest exercises the ADR-0029 defect directly: mentally reverting firstInheritableAncestor to blind epoch-1 sealing, to an unbounded walk-to-0, or to a walk that seals every skipped ancestor all fail the test's four assertions (zombie fenced, epoch 2 untouched, epoch 3's Seal byte-identical, CONTINUE names epoch 1, offsets resume at 3). LocalSequencerFailoverTest's moved counts (+1 gets, +2 total per takeover, uniformly across all four scenarios) match the production request pattern I traced by hand (one stat + one get from firstEntry() when the immediate predecessor is genuinely opened, since gets and stats are counted separately in StoreCounts/CountingBinStore) -- this is a tightening, not a weakening, and is fully disclosed in-line. One coverage gap found: the lower boundary of ChainReplay.firstInheritableAncestor's walk (chainEpoch >= 1) is never forced to actually decrement through epoch 1 to 0 -- no fixture burns every epoch back through and including epoch 1 -- so a `>=1` -> `>1` boundary mutation survives every test in this diff and, as far as I can find, every other test in the sequencer module. Traced the consequence by hand: it's a benign extra Seal write on an already-empty chain (equivalent to the 'seal every unsealed ancestor' candidate ADR-0029 rejected only on cost grounds, not safety), not an I2 violation, so I'm reporting it minor rather than major.

findings.title: firstInheritableAncestor's lower walk boundary is never exercised down to 0
findings.failure_scenario: Every test that reaches this method (LocalSequencerAncestorSealTest, and LocalSequencerFailoverTest's cost fixtures) has the genuine, non-burned ancestor sitting at epoch 1 itself, so the walk always finds a real CONTINUE and stops there before the boundary can matter -- both `>=1` and `>1` return the same value (1) in every fixture. No test burns epoch 1 itself (i.e., every epoch from the successor's predecessor down through and including epoch 1 is a burned/never-opened chain, epoch 0 being reserved and unleaseable). In that scenario correct code walks past chainEpoch==1 (non-origin, so neverOpened(null,false) is true) down to chainEpoch==0, returning 0 -- nothing to seal. The `>1` mutant stops at chainEpoch==1 without ever checking it and returns 1, so LocalSequencer.start would call recoverChainEnd()/seal() on a chain that was never opened. Traced by hand what that produces: CommitLog.seal on an empty chain (nextSequence=0, sealedAt=null) succeeds via putIfAbsent and writes a Seal(0, continuedAt) -- a real write with no correctness consequence, since there is no zombie leader to fence there, but it is still a behavior no test pins either way. Kill it with a fixture that burns every epoch from prevEpoch down through epoch 1 and asserts the successor's CONTINUE either points nowhere (prevEpoch==0, no predecessor sealed) or explicitly documents whatever the intended shape is.

notes: Verified by hand, not just by reading the comment: LocalSequencerFailoverTest's arithmetic. firstEntry() issues one stat() (present) then one get() (StoreCounts counts stats and gets separately in CountingBinStore), so a takeover whose immediate predecessor is genuinely opened (every fixture in this test) costs exactly +1 to gets() and +2 to total() versus the pre-M4.32 baseline -- matches every one of the six moved assertions (17->18, 45->46 gets; 26->28, 54->56, 18->20, 45->47 total) uniformly, consistent with the probe running once per takeover regardless of ancestor count or chain length as the comments claim.

check-test-integrity concern considered and dismissed: the LocalSequencerFailoverTest changes are all in the tightening direction (larger exact counts), not loosened tolerances, and each is accompanied by an inline reason -- not the 'production changed to satisfy the test' inversion.

TDD: check-tdd.sh already passed (per the packet), and I independently confirmed the primary assertion (zombie's next commit throws 'fenced') would fail under the exact defect ADR-0029 names (blind `epoch - 1` sealing), so the red record plausibly corresponds to the real defect rather than a compile error or a trivially-satisfiable assertion.
Tier is right: T1, MemoryBinStore, an injected FixedClock (no Thread.sleep, no wall clock) -- both files.

The ordering claim in LocalSequencer.start's comment ('seal before open crosses in, load-bearing') is not independently exercised by this sequential test -- there is no concurrent zombie write in flight during the crossing, so a hand-swap of seal-then-open to open-then-seal would likely still pass here. Not flagging as a blocking test gap: verifying that ordering needs a genuine concurrent race, which is the commit-protocol simulation's job (M4.13/M4.20/M4.19), not a T1 unit test's.

Acceptance criteria (zombie fenced, burned epochs untouched, offsets carry across, cost is +1 GET+STAT unconditionally) each have a test that would fail without the change -- no criterion found without coverage.
